niche: Psychology & human behavior (biases, habits, social dynamics)

ideas.title: Why You Can't Eat Without Watching Something
ideas.angle: Explains sensory pairing and cue-conditioned dopamine loops: your brain has linked the act of chewing with passive video consumption, making quiet eating feel agonizingly under-stimulating. It reveals how decoupling them resets your satiety signals.

hook.en: Stop eating until you find a video?

ideas.reason: Hyper-relatable everyday modern habit with millions of comments on TikTok and Reels admitting they let their food get cold searching for a video. High comment engagement and immediate self-identification drive retention.
sources: American Journal of Clinical Nutrition - Distracted eating and food intake
Journal of Behavioral Addictions - Conditioned smartphone checking and stimulus pairing

ideas.title: Why Doing Nothing Makes You Anxious
ideas.angle: Examines the Default Mode Network and 'idleness aversion': when you finally sit down to relax, your brain switches to self-evaluative background processing, interpreting stillness as falling behind. Explains how purposeful active rest silences the false alarm.

hook.en: Why does resting make you anxious?

ideas.reason: Massive cultural pain point among younger demographics suffering from chronic burnout and toxic productivity. Triggers intense emotional resonance and high shares to friends who struggle to unwind.
sources: Psychological Science - Idleness Aversion and the Need for Justification
Nature Reviews Neuroscience - The Brain's Default Mode Network

ideas.title: Why 4 Seconds of Silence Feels Agonizing
ideas.angle: Unpacks the 4-second conversational gap threshold: research shows that a pause longer than four seconds in casual dialogue triggers ancient social-exclusion fear circuitry in the amygdala, making silence feel three times longer than it actually is.

hook.en: Silence feels awkward in four seconds.

ideas.reason: Specific numbers in psychological hooks trigger intense curiosity. The video can physically demonstrate a calibrated 4-second pause, visually and auditorily gripping the viewer and proving the effect in real time.
sources: Journal of Experimental Social Psychology - Disrupting the flow: How brief silences in conversation affect social connection
Cognition - Timing and turn-taking in human conversation
